audit: 2026-09-17 scheduled remote agent: one 50 question batch across all four modules, published as seventeen files data/batches/sched_multi_topic_2026-09-17_a_NN.json. Split 13 Medicine, 13 Obstetrics and Gynaecology, 12 Paediatrics and 12 Psychiatry; tier mix 26 L3, 21 L4 and 3 L5 with no L1 and no L2, taking the bank to 6842 with Paediatrics on 1713, Obstetrics and Gynaecology on 1713, Psychiatry on 1703 and Medicine on 1713. Cell selection: the live matrix before this fire showed Paediatrics 1701, Obstetrics 1700, Medicine 1700 and Psychiatry 1691, with L3 deficits against the ideal 50 per cent of 13.02 points in Paediatrics, 12.59 in Obstetrics, 11.71 in Medicine and 11.03 in Psychiatry, L4 deficits against 45 per cent of 12.96, 12.53, 11.65 and 10.52 respectively, and L5 at 5.06 to 5.12 per cent in every module, a deficit of about minus 0.1 points. The strict per question argmax remains degenerate for the fifteenth consecutive fire: run literally it loads Paediatrics and Obstetrics and starves Psychiatry and Medicine, because the Medicine and Psychiatry L3 deficits sit 1.3 and 2.0 points behind the Paediatrics L3 leader and so never enter the 0.5 point near tie window. This fire therefore used the same resolution as the previous fourteen: the deficit ranking governs the weighting and the Section 2 module balance cap bounds the skew, implemented as a greedy per question argmax with a guard refusing any cell whose module total would exceed the lowest module total by more than 10, and near ties inside a module broken by an anti drift rule preferring the cell with fewer questions already allocated in this batch. That produced 26 L3 against 21 L4 rather than the near total L3 skew the raw argmax gives. L5 was held at 3 rather than the strict zero the argmax produces, because an all L3 and L4 batch decays the standing 5 per cent L5 share every fire; the 3 were placed in the three modules with the lowest live L5 share, namely Medicine, Psychiatry and Paediatrics. Final allocation 13/13/12/12 with the spread held at 10. Clusters were chosen by measuring live coverage density across candidate subtopics and taking the least covered: Medicine took reactive arthritis, prolactinoma, frailty before elective surgery, deprescribing after falls, opioid rotation in renal impairment, polymyalgia rheumatica, thyroid eye disease, acromegaly, ferritin interpretation, Lambert Eaton, cystic fibrosis related diabetes, eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis and AL amyloidosis; Paediatrics took thyroglossal duct cyst, congenital muscular torticollis, infant inguinal hernia, ankyloglossia, amblyopia, breath holding spells, Duchenne muscular dystrophy, Klinefelter syndrome, lambdoid synostosis, acquired subglottic stenosis, Alagille syndrome and congenital long QT syndrome; Psychiatry took premenstrual dysphoric disorder, expressed emotion and family intervention, advance statements, trichotillomania, gender affirming care, corticosteroid induced mania, narcolepsy, akathisia, drug induced QT prolongation, Huntington disease, isotretinoin and mood, and Wilson disease; Obstetrics and Gynaecology took postmenopausal osteoporosis, adenomyosis, overactive bladder, Bartholin abscess, permanent contraception counselling, endometrial ablation, tubo-ovarian abscess, vulvodynia, imperforate hymen, labial adhesions, actinomyces on cytology, suspected ovarian malignancy referral and obstetric anal sphincter injury. Audit: JSON valid, zero em-dashes, zero banned tokens, zero markdown asterisks, no L1 or L2, every stem written from the treating doctor's position, answer length ratio at or below 1.35 in all 50 questions (worst 1.22), every source_ref resolving to a label in the question's own sources array, at least two sources per question with an Australian source first, correct answer letters balanced at exactly 10 per letter, tags capped at 3 and all drawn from the live vocabulary with guideline names confined to sources, explanation summaries 3 to 5 sentences, key points 3 to 5, and pearls carrying named drugs, thresholds and timeframes. scripts/dupe_gate.py --new failed on the first Paediatrics run, flagging sched-0917a-paeds-006 (hip imaging for adolescent knee pain, 0.879 against sched-2026-09-08-p3-034) and sched-0917a-paeds-003 (ventilation tube referral threshold, 0.812 against paeds-gap9d-003); both were replaced outright with questions in the same cells on clusters with zero prior coverage, infant inguinal hernia and breath holding spells, and the gate then passed with 0 duplicates for all 50 against the 6792 existing questions. Note for the maintainer: the keyword coverage probe run before drafting did not catch either of these two, because it screened on cluster nouns such as grommet and Osgood rather than on the answer text the gate compares; the gate remains the only reliable check and was the sole reason both were caught.
